facts.statement: Researchers created a ZIF-8 nanocarrier designed to deliver the drug tectorigenin more effectively to treat muscle wasting.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: The study used two experimental setups: a lab model of starving muscle cells and a mouse model where the sciatic nerve was crushed to induce atrophy.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: In the cell model, the nanocarrier treatment restored muscle tube width to 92% of normal levels, which was much better than the drug given alone.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: In the mice, crushing the sciatic nerve caused the leg muscle mass to drop by 35% and the size of individual muscle fibers to shrink by 41%.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The nanocarrier treatment increased mouse muscle mass to 74% of normal levels and fiber size to 93%, while the drug alone did not produce significant recovery.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Mice treated with the nanocarrier showed better movement abilities compared to those treated with the drug alone after nerve injury.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors suggest the treatment works by calming specific breakdown systems in muscle cells, boosting protein building signals, and lowering oxidative stress and inflammation.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors conclude that this nanotechnology approach offers a promising strategy for treating muscle wasting caused by nerve damage.
facts.subject: other
